Munificent

myoo-NIF-uh-suhnt · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Munificent is more generous than necessary.

The retiring CEO's munificent bonus to every warehouse employee, not just the executives, made headlines across the industry.

Worked Example

When the small town's only factory nearly closed, an anonymous local businesswoman made a munificent offer to cover the workers' wages herself for an entire year while a buyer was found.

Covering an entire town's payroll out of pocket, with no obligation to do so, is a strikingly generous act -- exactly what munificent describes.

How Munificent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

bountiful

bountiful: giving or given in great abundance

lavish

lavish: very generous or extravagant in giving

Antonyms

stingy

stingy: unwilling to give or spend

miserly

miserly: hoarding money; extremely reluctant to spend

How Strong Is It? — generous → munificent → extravagant

generous vs. munificent

generous vs. munificent: willing to give freely, without necessarily giving an unusually large amount

extravagant vs. munificent

extravagant vs. munificent: spending or giving so much that it borders on excessive or reckless

Build the Word

The pieces

root — muni- (munus)

root — muni- (munus): gift, service, duty (Latin)

suffix — -ficent (-ficus + -ent)

suffix — -ficent (-ficus + -ent): making; possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Munificent traces back to the Latin munus, 'a gift or service,' combined with -ficent, 'making.' Something munificent is quite literally 'gift-making' -- generous almost by nature.

Use the root in a new word: remuneration

Use the root in a new word: remuneration: Her remuneration for the consulting project included both a flat fee and a share of the profits.

Root Check

Word Choice

Munificent describes the giver or the act of giving as remarkably generous. It's related to largesse (later in this unit), which names the generosity itself, especially when it flows from someone with power or wealth to those with less.
